---
title: Data API grants
description: Grant new tables to the Supabase Data API roles in the same migration.
navigation:
  icon: i-lucide-key-square
---

From 2026-10-30, Supabase stops granting Data API access to new tables in `public` on its own. A table with no grant answers "permission denied" (`42501`) to supabase-js, PostgREST, and GraphQL.

Row level security does not help here. Postgres checks the grant first.

## Rules for every layer

- A migration that creates a table in `public` grants the table in the same file. Use the next numbered file, and never edit a shipped file.
- Grant the smallest set that the policies need. Do not copy a broad template.
- `anon` gets `select` only. It gets it only on a table with an anon or public select policy.
- `authenticated` gets only the privileges that its policies allow. `profiles` has a select policy and no update policy on purpose, so it gets `select` only.
- `service_role` gets `select, insert, update, delete`.
- Never grant `truncate`, `references`, `trigger`, or `all`.
- Use identity columns (`generated ... as identity`), not `serial`. An identity column needs no sequence grant. A `serial` column needs `grant usage on sequence ...` for an insert through the API.
- A new function that the API calls gets `grant execute on function ... to <roles>`.
- A `grant` is additive. Write the file so it is safe to run twice.

Each layer has a unit test, `test/data-api-grants.test.ts`. It fails when a table has no grant to `authenticated`, when `anon` has more than `select`, or when a file grants a banned privilege.

```sql [db/migrations/NNN_my_table_grants.sql]
grant select on public.my_table to anon;
grant select, insert, update, delete on public.my_table to authenticated;
grant select, insert, update, delete on public.my_table to service_role;
```

## Grant files in the shipped layers

The baselines were written when Supabase granted every new table automatically. These files add the grants for a new database:

| Layer | File |
| --- | --- |
| `supabase` | `006_data_api_grants.sql` |
| `supabase-shop` | `005_data_api_grants.sql` |
| `supabase-storage` | `005_data_api_grants.sql` |
| `supabase-blog` | `004_data_api_grants.sql` |

They change nothing on an older database, which already holds broader privileges. The runner applies them right after the baseline on a fresh install.

If the role in `DATABASE_URL` does not own the tables, `grant` only warns, and the file is still recorded. Check the result with `has_table_privilege`.

## Restricted reads

`007_restrict_staff_reads.sql` narrows four read policies:

- `settings` is readable by staff. Staff is a user with at least one capability, checked through `my_capabilities()`.
- `pluto_migrations`, `roles`, and `role_capabilities` are readable by `is_admin()` only.

A plain signed-up user reads none of them. `dashboard_user` keeps its read access on `settings` and `pluto_migrations`.

`006_data_api_grants.sql` also grants `execute` on `is_admin()`, `has_capability(text)`, and `my_capabilities()` to `authenticated` and `service_role`, and on `set_my_locale(text)` to `authenticated`. It does not revoke the default `public` execute, because policies that apply to `anon` still call these functions.
